# Working for Workers Six Act

The Working For Workers Six Act, 2024 () is an act of the Legislative Assembly of Ontario relating to labour rights.
Provisions
The act invests up to  in training more than one million workers through the Skills Development Fund. The act also outlines new standards for immigration representatives.
The legislation amends the Employment Standards Act (ESA), so that employees who have worked for a given employer for 13 consecutive weeks are allowed to take 27 weeks of unpaid illness leave within a 52-week period.
The act introduces a significant mandatory fine for a second or subsequent offence under the Occupational Health and Safety Act (OHSA).
The act imposes a requirement for properly fitting personal protective equipment to. be provided to women across all sectors, building on a similar requirement on the construction industry in the Working for Workers Act, 2023.
The legislation requires that employees who become parents through adoption or surrogacy be entitled to 16 weeks of unpaid parental leave.
The provincial Chief Prevention Officer is assigned additional powers including the ability to assess whether a training program delivered outside of Ontario is equivalent to one approved under OHSA.
